title: Financial adaptations persist across health direction and do not define recovery alone
source_unit: Recontacted SHED adult respondent, paired 2024 and 2025 waves

denominator.unit: paired respondents with valid health direction and 2025 panel weight

observations.method: Weighted same-respondent SHED panel transition; 2025 Yes share conditional on 2024 Yes, by ordinal self-rated-health direction.
observations.subgroup: Respondents with worsened self-rated health; adaptation-specific 2024 adopter universe.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors; annual self-report, recontact selection, and metric-specific valid denominators apply.
observations.counterinterpretation: Health worsening may reflect or share causes with financial adaptation; persistence is not a health effect.

denominator.unit: paired respondents with valid health direction and 2025 panel weight

observations.method: Weighted same-respondent SHED panel transition; 2025 Yes share conditional on 2024 Yes, by ordinal self-rated-health direction.
observations.subgroup: Respondents with unchanged self-rated health; adaptation-specific 2024 adopter universe.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors; unchanged health does not mean unchanged illness, care, prices, income, or debt.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable self-rated health can coexist with changing financial conditions and adaptations.

denominator.unit: paired respondents with valid health direction and 2025 panel weight

observations.method: Weighted same-respondent SHED panel transition; 2025 Yes share conditional on 2024 Yes, by ordinal self-rated-health direction.
observations.subgroup: Respondents with improved self-rated health; adaptation-specific 2024 adopter universe.
observations.uncertainty: No design-based standard errors; improved self-rated health is not a dated treatment or financial recovery measure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Health improvement can coexist with persistent debt, delayed consumption, care obligations, or other constraints.

boundary: Descriptive same-respondent panel comparison. It does not establish causality, a dated health or price shock, care intensity, payment burden, or later trust, remedy, or political action.
